title: Basis on Which an Appraisal Fee Is Taken Off, Belrose Appraisal and Gemological Services
content:
# Basis on Which a Fee Is Taken Off

A fee already charged under Belrose Appraisal and Gemological Services is taken off where the appraisal was bundled with an upgrade or a commission the customer went ahead with, or where the chain charged twice for the same line. A fee is taken off only when no amount has already been taken off that same fee line. The credit is recorded against the fee line it answers, so a customer who was charged for several lines can see which of them was given back. A fee is never taken off merely because the customer is disappointed with the value the report states, because the value is the appraiser's professional opinion and not a priced service outcome.

Whether the fee is credited when the piece is traded up at the chain, and whether it is credited when a commission is placed on the back of the report, are fixed per service.

## Whether a credit already stands

Before a fee is taken off, the engagement's own records are read for any amount already taken off that same fee line. An amount already taken off the line under any reason the records carry, whether bundled with an upgrade, bundled with a commission, service recovery or duplicate charge, means no further amount is taken off that line. The records decide; the customer's recollection of whether a credit was given does not.

## Questions answered

**The customer went ahead with an upgrade the appraisal was bundled with. Is the fee taken off?** Yes, at a service whose fee is credited against a trade-up, and the credit is recorded against the fee line it answers.

**The customer was charged the same line twice.** The chain charged twice for the same line, so the fee is taken off, recorded against the fee line that was charged in error.

**A credit was already recorded against the fee line last month, and the customer asks for it again.** No further amount is taken off that fee line; a fee is taken off only when no amount has already been taken off that same line.

**The customer is unhappy that the report values the piece below what they paid.** The fee is not taken off on that ground. The value is the appraiser's professional opinion and not a priced service outcome.

**The customer was charged for several lines and asks which was given back.** The credit is recorded against the fee line it answers, and that line is the one given back.
